tips.cue: Drupes whitish and firm on a fresh cluster.
tips.collect: Take only from current-season clusters - the plant holds grey, empty fruit from previous years all the way through winter and spring.
tips.handling: Rub off the waxy coat, then scarify.
tips.caution: This is the species that most badly misleads a calendar-based model. Persistent old fruit generates fruiting records year-round; judge by cluster condition, not by date.

tips.cue: Schizocarp segments brown and parting from the axis.
tips.collect: Roll discs gently between fingers.
tips.handling: Scarify before sowing.

tips.cue: Berries fully coloured and slightly soft.
tips.collect: Hand-pick whole berries.
tips.handling: Macerate and float off pulp. Most require both scarification and stratification, and are slow and unreliable from seed.

tips.cue: Berries fully coloured and slightly soft.
tips.collect: Hand-pick whole berries.
tips.handling: Macerate and float off pulp. Most require both scarification and stratification, and are slow and unreliable from seed.

tips.collect: Roll discs gently between fingers.
tips.handling: Scarify before sowing.

tips.cue: Berries fully coloured and sticky-firm.
tips.collect: Hand-pick clusters.
tips.handling: Clean pulp, then scarify and treat with heat or smoke. Manzanitas are notoriously difficult from seed; propagate from cuttings if you have the option.

tips.cue: Calyces dry and brown, nutlets dark and hard inside.
tips.collect: Bend the stalk over a bag and tap - ripe nutlets fall out cleanly.
tips.handling: Winnow chaff gently; nutlets are small and blow away easily.

tips.cue: Calyces dry and brown, nutlets dark and hard inside.
tips.collect: Bend the stalk over a bag and tap - ripe nutlets fall out cleanly.
tips.handling: Winnow chaff gently; nutlets are small and blow away easily.

tips.cue: Pomes fully red and slightly soft. Orange-red is still immature.
tips.collect: Clip whole clusters. Fruit persists well past ripeness, so late in the season check that seed inside is plump and dark, not shrivelled.
tips.handling: Macerate and float off pulp. Cold-moist stratify 1-3 months. Fresh seed germinates readily.

tips.cue: Long ribbed capsule turns straw-coloured and the seed inside is dark brown-black.
tips.collect: Capsules fire explosively and the window is only a few days per capsule. Bag developing capsules or collect daily.
tips.handling: Dry in a paper bag and let them self-thresh. No pretreatment needed.
tips.caution: This species flowers and fruits nearly year-round in mild coastal sites, so the modelled window is much wider than any single population's.

tips.cue: Calyces dry and brown, nutlets dark and hard inside.
tips.collect: Bend the stalk over a bag and tap - ripe nutlets fall out cleanly.
tips.handling: Winnow chaff gently; nutlets are small and blow away easily.

tips.cue: Pods leathery to papery and turning brown; seeds rattle loose inside.
tips.collect: Many pods dehisce explosively - bag whole infructescences before they twist open, or check plants every few days.
tips.handling: Hard-coated seed benefits from scarification before sowing. Freeze or heat-treat to kill bruchid beetle larvae, which are common.

tips.cue: Capsule dry, brown, and beginning to split; seed black and flat.
tips.collect: Tip the capsule into a bag - ripe seed pours out.
tips.handling: Easy to clean and store. Long juvenile period - expect years to flowering.

tips.cue: Drupes deep red and sticky.
tips.collect: Strip clusters by hand.
tips.handling: Wash off the sticky exudate, then scarify. Slow and uneven to germinate.

tips.cue: Berries fully coloured and slightly soft.
tips.collect: Hand-pick whole berries.
tips.handling: Macerate and float off pulp. Most require both scarification and stratification, and are slow and unreliable from seed.

tips.cue: Fruit fully coloured and slightly yielding.
tips.collect: Use tongs. Glochids are the real hazard, not the spines.
tips.handling: Macerate, rinse, dry thoroughly.

tips.cue: Acorn caps release cleanly and the nut is fully coloured; green acorns still tight in the cap are immature.
tips.collect: Collect from the ground within a day or two of drop, or pick mature acorns directly.
tips.handling: Float-test and discard floaters and any with weevil exit holes. Oak acorns are recalcitrant - they must not dry out. Sow promptly or refrigerate moist.

tips.cue: Varies with fruit type - fleshy fruits fully coloured and slightly soft, dry achenes brown and loose.
tips.collect: Pick fleshy fruit by hand; strip plumed achenes when they detach at a touch.
tips.handling: Clean pulp from fleshy fruit promptly - fermenting flesh kills seed. Most need cold-moist stratification.

tips.cue: Berries fully blue with a waxy bloom, and soft.
tips.collect: Clip whole umbels. Birds strip a plant in days once ripe.
tips.handling: Macerate and float off pulp the same day. Warm then cold stratify.

tips.cue: Capsule dry and papery, splitting along the seams; seed flat and dark.
tips.collect: Tip capsules into a bag.
tips.handling: Easy to clean and store. Expect four or more years from seed to flower.
tips.caution: Several Calochortus species are rare or narrowly endemic. Check status before collecting.

tips.handling: Clean pulp from fleshy fruit promptly - fermenting flesh kills seed. Most need cold-moist stratification.

tips.cue: Pappus (the fluff) has dried and begun to lift; heads look grey and open rather than green and tight.
tips.collect: Tug lightly - ripe achenes release with almost no resistance. If you have to pull, come back in a week.
tips.handling: Dries fast. Rub heads over a screen to separate achenes from chaff; many species have a high proportion of empty seed, so check fill by pinching.

tips.cue: Drupes fully coloured and firm; on sumacs the sticky coating has developed.

tips.handling: Break apart over a bag. Fill rate is often low - check for plump achenes.

tips.collect: Clip whole umbels into a bag.
tips.handling: Dry and rub apart.
tips.caution: This family includes poison hemlock and water hemlock, both lethally toxic. Do not collect from an umbellifer you have not identified with certainty.

tips.collect: Tug lightly - ripe achenes release with almost no resistance. If you have to pull, come back in a week.
tips.handling: Dries fast. Rub heads over a screen to separate achenes from chaff; many species have a high proportion of empty seed, so check fill by pinching.

tips.cue: Pods leathery to papery and turning brown; seeds rattle loose inside.
tips.collect: Many pods dehisce explosively - bag whole infructescences before they twist open, or check plants every few days.
tips.handling: Hard-coated seed benefits from scarification before sowing. Freeze or heat-treat to kill bruchid beetle larvae, which are common.

tips.cue: Drupes fully coloured and firm; on sumacs the sticky coating has developed.
tips.collect: Strip clusters by hand. Watch that fruit persists long after ripening - old grey fruit from last season is often still attached.
tips.handling: Remove the fleshy or waxy coat. Hard seed coat usually needs scarification.
tips.caution: Confirm identity - this family includes poison oak, whose fruit is also collected by birds and looks superficially similar at a distance.

tips.cue: Berries fully coloured and slightly soft.
tips.collect: Hand-pick whole berries.
tips.handling: Macerate and float off pulp. Most require both scarification and stratification, and are slow and unreliable from seed.

tips.cue: Flower clusters dry to rusty brown and achenes are firm.
tips.collect: Strip clusters into a bag.
tips.handling: Very small seed with a lot of chaff. Germination is erratic without fire-related cues such as smoke or charate treatment.

tips.cue: Berries fully red and warty-firm.
tips.collect: Do not collect.
tips.caution: CNPS rare-plant ranked and locally restricted. Enjoy it in place; seed collection from wild populations is not appropriate.

tips.cue: Capsules dry and beginning to split at the tip.
tips.collect: Strip upward into a bag before the plumed seed disperses.
tips.handling: Screen out the fluff. Very small seed - use a fine sieve.

tips.cue: Fruit fully coloured and slightly yielding.
tips.collect: Use tongs. Glochids are the real hazard, not the spines.
tips.handling: Macerate, rinse, dry thoroughly.

tips.cue: Acorn caps release cleanly and the nut is fully coloured; green acorns still tight in the cap are immature.
tips.collect: Collect from the ground within a day or two of drop, or pick mature acorns directly.
tips.handling: Float-test and discard floaters and any with weevil exit holes. Oak acorns are recalcitrant - they must not dry out. Sow promptly or refrigerate moist.

tips.cue: Coils uncurled and dry, nutlets hard.
tips.collect: Strip the uncurled coil into a bag.
tips.handling: Nutlets shed easily and are often lost to timing - check plants frequently.

tips.handling: Nutlets shed easily and are often lost to timing - check plants frequently.

tips.cue: Capsules papery and brown; seed hard and dark.
tips.collect: Pick capsules directly.
tips.handling: Hard coat - scarify.

tips.handling: Macerate, float, then cold stratify.

tips.collect: Rub heads between palms over a bag.
tips.handling: High chaff fraction is normal and mostly harmless for direct sowing.
tips.caution: Buckwheats hold dried flower heads for months after seed has dropped, so a brown head is not proof of full seed.

tips.cue: Capsules splitting and cotton visible.
tips.collect: Collect the instant capsules open - viability is measured in days.
tips.handling: Sow immediately on wet mineral soil. Do not attempt to store.

tips.cue: Florets straw-coloured, seed firm; awns twist when dry.
tips.collect: Strip the seed head upward through a closed hand into a bag. Ripe seed shatters readily - a light shake tells you.
tips.handling: Keep well ventilated. Awned grasses tangle badly; leave awns on unless you are sowing with a drill.
